title: One Thousand and One Nights (Alf layla wa-layla)
summary: The One Thousand and One Nights is a collection of tales drawing on Persian, Indian, Greek, Turkish and Central Asian elements, Arabized for a Middle Eastern audience. The Library of Congress places its earliest manuscript tradition in 9th-century Baghdad, followed by Syrian and Egyptian traditions; the earliest Arabic manuscript found so far dates only from the 14th or 15th century. This is a growing oral and written tradition, not a single dated composition.

uncertainty.note: The 9th century refers to the tradition, not a surviving manuscript: Cambridge gives the earliest Arabic manuscript found as 14th or 15th century and the earliest Genizah manuscript as 13th century.

importance.justification: A foundational work of Arabic story-telling, translated into French in the early 18th century and later across Europe.

sources.title: A Thousand and One Nights: Arabian Story-telling in World Literature

reviewer_note: Tradition, not an event: 9th-century Baghdad rests on the Library of Congress wording about the manuscript tradition; no surviving 9th-century manuscript was cited by an opened page. The pin is Baghdad as named by LOC, with the full range of origins (Persia, India, Syria, Egypt) recorded in the summary. Dated by tradition; the id's 0850 is a label.
